findings.title: Delay damages of $4,200 a day, no cap, on top of actual damages
findings.quote: if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
findings.explanation: The clause charges 2% of the whole $210,000 contract value for every calendar day a delivery date is missed: 2% x $210,000 = $4,200 a day, or $29,400 a week. Nothing in Article 11 caps it, and §11.3 says it is on top of Harrington's right to recover actual damages and lets Harrington deduct it from payments. The clock runs until Harrington accepts the deliverable, and acceptance is never deemed to happen by the passage of time (§3.3), so it also runs while Harrington is testing (up to 30 days under §3.1). At $4,200 a day the charge equals the entire contract value after 50 days ($210,000 / $4,200).

register_refs.quote: 9.1 If the Supplier fails to achieve any Key Date, the Supplier shall pay to the Customer liquidated damages in the amount of one per cent (1%) of the Contract Value for each day or part day by which the relevant Key Date is missed.
5.2 The Supplier shall meet each Key Date. Time shall be of the essence in respect of the Key Dates.

findings.title: AtliQ's liability is unlimited; Harrington's is capped at what it has paid
findings.quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE CONTRACTOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING CONTRACTOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF THE BAA, OR ANY DATA SECURITY INCIDENT.
findings.explanation: There is no ceiling on what AtliQ Inc can owe, including indirect losses, indemnity payments, a BAA breach or any data security incident. The clause is one-sided: §10.1 stops Harrington being liable to AtliQ for indirect losses and lost profit, and §10.2 caps Harrington's liability at the fees it has actually paid. The BAA adds its own 'no limitation' wording (BAA §8.2).

The text does not say which AtliQ materials would go into this platform; that is a question for a person.

findings.title: MSA allows offshore staff on de-identified data; the BAA does not
findings.quote: No PHI shall be accessed, stored or processed outside the United States without Client's prior written consent. Any Contractor Personnel located outside the United States shall access only de-identified data within Client-controlled environments.
findings.explanation: MSA §12.4 leaves two routes open: PHI offshore with Harrington's written consent, and offshore staff on de-identified data. BAA §4.1 bans PHI outside the US with no consent route, and BAA §4.2 says every approved subcontractor must be a US-organized entity with all personnel in the US. BAA §1.5 counts any Affiliate as a Subcontractor, so AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd (Pune) would be one. The MSA says the BAA controls 'with respect to PHI' (§12.1, §15.10) but is silent on de-identified data. Which document governs Pune's access to de-identified data is a possible conflict, for counsel.

findings.title: 24-hour incident notice to Harrington vs 2 business days from Pune; costs uncapped
findings.quote: Contractor shall notify Client of any actual or reasonably suspected security incident affecting Client data within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery and shall bear all costs of investigation, notification, credit monitoring and remediation.
findings.explanation: AtliQ Inc must notify Harrington within 24 hours (MSA §12.3; BAA §5.1 by phone and in writing). The BAA treats an event as discovered when any Subcontractor knows of it, and its Subcontractor definition includes Affiliates. AtliQ's own intercompany BAA gives Pune 2 business days to report to AtliQ Inc (§5.1). A weekend or two business days can therefore pass inside Pune before AtliQ Inc hears of it while Harrington's 24 hours is running. The costs AtliQ bears under §12.3 are not capped (§10.3).

findings.title: Harrington can end on 7 days' notice and pay nothing for work in progress
findings.quote: Client may terminate this Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, for any reason or no reason, upon seven (7) days' written notice to Contractor. Upon such termination, Client's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by Client prior to the effective date of termination; Client shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.
findings.explanation: Only Harrington has a convenience exit; AtliQ can end only for uncured breach (§5.2). On exit AtliQ must hand over all Deliverables 'whether complete or incomplete' at once (§5.5(a)) and is paid only for accepted ones. Example: Milestone 2 ($60,000, due at week 14) is in build and Harrington gives 7 days' notice: the clause leaves $0 owing for that work, though the incomplete Deliverable is handed over. The checklist says 'they pay for work done'.
